title: Modification of a Chlamydomonas reinhardtii CRISPR/Cas9 transformation protocol for use with widely available electroporation equipment
author: Park, Asbury, et al.
materials: Cells were grown to a density between 0.8–2.5 × 106 cells/mL. 4 × 106 cells were collected per electroporation trial and centrifuged for 8 min at 2000 rcf in a 15-mL conical tube. The pellet was resuspended in TAP-sucrose medium, to a final cell density of 100 × 106 cells/mL and the suspension was transferred into a 1.5-mL microtube. The cells were heat shocked in an Eppendorf Thermomixer at 40 °C for 30 min, 350 rpm, then incubated for 5–10 min at room temperature. 40 µL of the final cell suspension (4 × 106 cells) was pipetted into a 0.2 cm gap cuvette, followed by the uncut Cas9 expression vector plasmid (pPH187) and the PSY1 sgRNA expression vector plasmid or the empty sgRNA expression vector (pPH331 or pPH339). Plasmid concentrations were between 0.2–1.0 µg/µL.

Exponential pulses were produced by a Bio-Rad Gene Pulser II electroporator. The external resistance was set to ∞ (infinite, open circuit) and the external capacitance was set to 25 µF. The resistance of the cuvette with the cells and plasmids was between 300 and 400Ω. These conditions produced a tau of ~10 ms. A second exponential pulse was applied 2–5 s after the first pulse. Many other electroporators can produce the exponential waveform shown in Fig. 1(B).Fig. 1Waveforms used to electroporate Cas9 and sgRNA expression vectors into C. reinhardtii. (a) Published NEPA21 Super Electroporator waveform[1]. (b) Exponential waveform generated for electroporation by the Bio-Rad Gene Pulser II.Fig 1

5–10 s after electroporation, 500 µL of TAP-Arg was pipetted into each cuvette. After all the electroporations were completed, the cell suspensions were then pipetted into a 24-well plate. The well plate was then sealed with parafilm and covered with aluminum foil to keep the cultures in the dark. The plates were initially incubated at 31–33 °C for 22–24 h. We then incubated for an additional 22–24 h at room temperature, 21–25 °C, on an orbital shaker (120 rpm). The cells were then spread onto three TAP-Arginine-Yeast-Tryptone-paromomycin plates (160 µL cell culture per plate). steps.title: Prepare starter cultures
steps.instruction: Grow C. reinhardtii strain CC‑3403 in 50 mL TAP‑Arg medium in 125 mL flasks, shaking at 120 rpm, at 21–25 °C with a 14 h light/10 h dark cycle (10–15 µE m⁻² s⁻¹). Sub‑culture every 3–4 days at a 50:1 or 100:1 dilution to maintain exponential growth.

steps.title: Harvest cells for electroporation
steps.instruction: When culture density reaches 0.8–2.5 × 10⁶ cells mL⁻¹, collect 4 × 10⁶ cells per trial, centrifuge 8 min at 2000 rcf in a 15 mL conical tube, resuspend pellet in TAP‑sucrose medium to 100 × 10⁶ cells mL⁻¹, and transfer the suspension to a 1.5 mL microtube.

steps.title: Heat‑shock cells
steps.instruction: Heat‑shock the cell suspension in an Eppendorf Thermomixer at 40 °C, 350 rpm for 30 min, then let stand at room temperature for 5–10 min.

steps.title: Add DNA to cuvette
steps.instruction: Pipette 40 µL of the heat‑shocked cell suspension (≈4 × 10⁶ cells) into a 0.2 cm gap electroporation cuvette. Add the uncut Cas9 expression vector (pPH187) and the PSY1 sgRNA vector (pPH331 or pPH339). Use plasmid concentrations of 0.2–1.0 µg µL⁻¹, delivering 1 µg or 2 µg sgRNA plasmid and 2 µg or 4 µg Cas9 plasmid as desired.

steps.title: Electroporate cells
steps.instruction: Electroporate using a Bio‑Rad Gene Pulser II set to an exponential waveform: external resistance infinite, external capacitance 25 µF, cuvette resistance 300–400 Ω (τ≈10 ms). Apply a first pulse, then a second pulse 2–5 s later.

steps.title: Recover cells post‑electroporation
steps.instruction: 5–10 s after the second pulse, add 500 µL TAP‑Arg to the cuvette, then transfer the entire cell suspension to a 24‑well plate. Seal each well with parafilm and wrap in aluminum foil. Incubate 22–24 h at 31–33 °C, then a further 22–24 h at 21–25 °C on an orbital shaker at 120 rpm.

steps.title: Plate on selective agar
steps.instruction: Spread 160 µL of the recovered culture onto each of three 100‑mm TAP‑Arginine‑Yeast‑Tryptone‑paromomycin plates (1.5 % agar, TAP + 100 mg L⁻¹ arginine + 3 mg mL⁻¹ yeast extract + 2 mg mL⁻¹ tryptone + 10 mg mL⁻¹ paromomycin). Keep plates in the dark at room temperature for 19–25 days to allow colonies to develop. (Plates lacking yeast extract and tryptone were also tested.)

steps.title: Count colonies
steps.instruction: Colonies become visible after 7–10 days; final counting can be performed after 19–25 days of incubation.
